title: Metric Faucet: ingress governor for high-cardinality inference KPIs
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: sudden bursts of high-cardinality metrics from per-tenant/per-route inference requests are overwhelming the metrics ingestion pipeline (OTel -> aggregator -> Prometheus adapter). This manifests as ingest queues increasing latency, cardinality explosions in downstream TSDBs, and higher cloud bills. Root cause analysis shows unbounded label permutations from session-scoped tags and ephemeral request IDs.

Goal: implement a lightweight, deployable "metric faucet" (ingress governor) that sits in front of the metric ingestion path to enforce adaptive thinning and budget-aware admission for inference KPIs while preserving useful signal for SLOing and debugging. The component must: (1) limit cardinality growth, (2) surface backpressure to callers, (3) keep trace↔metric linkage for top-N samples, and (4) be incrementally deployable and observable.

Design summary: the faucet will perform per-tenant and per-route admission using configurable budgets. Strategies include deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by canonicalized label sets, early aggregation for well-known ephemeral labels (session_id, request_token), and histogram sketching for latency distributions. A tracing hook will mark sampled events with sampling_id and forward trace IDs in OTLP spans so we can reconstruct sample context in traces. The faucet exposes metrics on dropped-by-reason, sampling-rate-per-tenant, canonicalization-misses, and ingress-latency.

Acceptance criteria: end-to-end token-cost and ingestion throughput reduced by >=35% on synthetic high-cardinality traffic; no regression in 99th latency SLO for metric delivery; sampled metric-to-trace correlation available for >95% of sampled spans in staging.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary in prod telemetry ingress (10% of tenants), validate savings and debug fidelity, then ramp 10->30->100% with per-tenant opt-outs. Backfill older metrics with aggregated rollups where appropriate.

notes_on_tradeoffs: We trade absolute fidelity for cardinality control. Deterministic sampling preserves reproducibility of samples but loses tail signal for very-low-frequency labels. Early aggregation reduces ingestion but obfuscates per-request debugging; therefore we keep a small deterministic sample and link samples to traces to recover context when needed. Complexity: adds a new runtime component; to mitigate, we implement faucet as a sidecar-enabled module deployable behind feature flag.
qa_plan: Unit tests for sampler determinism and canonicalizer. Integration tests: replay trace+metric recording to staging ingress verifying that sampled metrics have corresponding OTLP spans with sampling_id. Load test: 1M metrics/sec synthetic client to validate throughput and drop ratios. Verify dashboards for dropped_reasons, sampling_rate and end-to-end latency.
